items.followUp: Define a bonding pair of electrons and give one example.

rubric.why: Identifies that a lone pair consists of two electrons that are not shared in a bond.
rubric.description: Defines a lone pair as a pair of valence electrons not shared in a chemical bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example and identifies the lone pair(s) in it.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of a lone pair, such as the two lone pairs on oxygen in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example.

modelAnswer: A lone pair is a pair of valence electrons on an atom that is not shared with another atom in a chemical bond.
For example, the oxygen atom in a water molecule has two lone pairs.

rubric.description: States that 24-carat gold is pure gold.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as pure gold.

rubric.why: Gives the gold content of 24-carat gold.
rubric.description: States that all 24 parts out of 24 are gold, or that it is 100% gold.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct composition.

modelAnswer: It contains 24 parts of gold out of 24 parts, so it is 100% gold.

rubric.why: Defines the ionic bond as the attraction between ions of opposite charge.
rubric.description: Defines an ionic bond as the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: Identifies the transfer of one electron from sodium to chlorine.
rubric.description: Shows that a sodium atom transfers one outer electron to a chlorine atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct electron transfer.

rubric.why: Identifies the ions formed and their opposite charges.
rubric.description: Shows the formation of Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both ions with the correct charges.

rubric.why: Shows in the dot-and-cross model that chlorine has a complete outer shell after gaining the electron.
rubric.description: Shows the transferred electron and the completed outer shell of the chloride ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct dot-and-cross outer shell with eight electrons.

rubric.why: Gives the balanced equation for forming sodium chloride.
rubric.description: Writes the balanced formation equation for sodium chloride.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct balanced equation and product.

modelAnswer: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions.
A sodium atom transfers its one outer electron to a chlorine atom.
Dot-and-cross model (× is sodium's electron; • are chlorine's electrons):
The chloride ion has a complete octet: seven dots and the transferred cross.
